implementation.scope: 10 L3 command adapters over one shared settings domain: prongs, prong editor, surface prong, metal piece, channel border, bead on curve, bead on surface, pull to rail, row end modes and the settings mass read-out.
implementation.shared_input: settings::gems::GemRow built from the gem owner's om9.gem records
implementation.shared_output: prong/bead/metal bodies with the om9.settings.prong payload; mass through metal_weight

manual_gate.note: no human UI review is claimed; the dashboard keeps the 10 L3 at WIP until a reviewer signs

limitations: 4 Prongs Close builds the sheet's closer pair: both North-side prongs sit inside the 4 Prongs 0 spacing and stay two distinct prongs.
A selection without gem objects is refused: the builder consumes the shared gem row instead of guessing.
A tight row can put the facing prongs of two stones on one point; the builder merges that pair into one shared prong and reports merged_prongs rather than refusing the style.
Border=On consumes the last committed channel border; the app never re-derives a border from the row.
Corner smoothing is the documented 0..1 angle; the exact Matrix corner radius law is not verified.
Count and Spacing are alternatives: setting one clears the other, and the last bead sits on the end fraction.
Curve mode needs a curve: it follows the picked curve, or the committed channel border with Border=On; with neither it is a typed Missing('metal piece curve'), never a row-offset body.
Cutter features are committed as bodies but never weighed; the report counts them under excluded_cutters.
Drop is negative-up per the sheet wording; the UI still has to confirm the sign on the preview.
F4 direction falls back to world +Z at the world centre.
Only a selected circle rail is accepted; an arc or line rail returns a typed refusal.
SettingsMass is a text command without a toolbar slot; mass covers settings features committed in this session.
The base bead diameter is 1.0 mm (OM9 engineering default); the sheet only gives the scale.
The editor rebuilds from the om9.settings.prong payload; a body without it is refused rather than re-derived.
These are command options, not a toolbar icon; the record says so instead of inventing an icon id.
